local_articles.title: Is Rodrigo De Paul injured? Why the Inter Miami star isn't playing against Chicago Fire FC
local_articles.snippet: Rodrigo De Paul is expected to miss Inter Miami's MLS match against Chicago Fire FC as the club manages his workload following Argentina's run to the 2026 FIFA World Cup final. Inter Miami has opted not to rush the Argentine midfielder back into action, in line with FIFA and FIFPRO's player welfare recommendations after a demanding international campaign. FIFA and FIFPRO agreed on a set of player welfare measures in 2025 aimed at protecting players from excessive workloads. The recommendations include: A minimum 72-hour gap between matches. A recommended 21-day offseason or recovery period following the end of a player's season. The governing bodies also said the recovery period should be managed individually by each club and player, depending on the match schedule and any applicable collective agreements. questions.title: Who will President Donald Trump nominate in 2026 to succeed Marty Makary as FDA commissioner?
questions.background: Marty Makary resigned as commissioner of the US Food and Drug Administration in May 2026, leaving the position vacant. The president nominates the commissioner, subject to Senate confirmation.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official presidential announcement or reliable news reporting directly quoting that announcement. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the first person President Trump publicly announces as his nominee for FDA commissioner after Makary’s May 2026 resignation and before the end of 2026. The nomination announcement is sufficient; Senate confirmation is not required. Accepted Answer Format : The nominee’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Marty Makary resigned as FDA commissioner on May 12, 2026 following pushback from HHS Secretary RFK Jr., pharma stakeholders, vaping lobbyists, and anti-abortion groups, with Deputy Commissioner for Human Foods Kyle Diamantas named Acting Commissioner. Diamantas—a close friend of Donald Trump Jr., senior counselor to RFK Jr., pro-life advocate, and widely praised by career staff and industry as a stabilizing leader—is the clear individual frontrunner (~28%) despite lacking an M.D. Other plausible RFK Jr.-compatible picks include HHS Deputy Secretary Jim O'Neill, former Acting FDA chief Sara Brenner, Florida Surgeon General Joseph Ladapo, and FDA biologics leader Vinay Prasad, while roughly 51% remains on an unannounced outside physician, healthcare executive, or former lawmaker.
